label: prf:six-term-per-derivation-weights
title: Proof of six term per derivation weights
html:
Proof. The constituent baseline Z\,m_{\mathfrak{p}} + N\,m_{\mathfrak{n}} + Z\,m_e is the free-particle sum from CODATA. The binding energy is the algebraic difference of the bound atom's mass formula and its free baseline. Each of the six terms contributes additively to the categorical mass per unified six-term decomposition; isolating the physical scale of each contribution is exactly the per-derivation reading above:

  • T_1 binding (descended Markov): the categorical mass formula \mathfrak{m}(Z, N) = E_{0,\beta} \cdot \mathfrak{m}(\beta_{Z,N}) with E_{0,\beta} = 0.7823 MeV the free-neutron β-decay Q per categorical mass, Markov reads T_1 in cat units. The binding contribution is the bound–free differential.
  • T_2 + T_3 binding (brane tower): per the atomic-braid mass formula in the Particles chapter, the binding correction is \alpha \cdot \sum_i \ln\lvert \hat V_i \rvert where \alpha = m_e \cdot 8G is the Borromean–Catalan binding scale and G \approx 0.9160 is Catalan's constant. Per the mass-endomorphism tower, \alpha\,\ln\lvert V \rvert is the leading-order expansion of -\alpha\,\mathrm{Li}_2^q(-\lvert V \rvert), so the same \alpha scale governs both the leading-order and the corrected q-dilogarithm form.
  • T_4 binding (Frobenius co-Casimir): the universal Frobenius co-Casimir T_4 = m_e \cdot \tau(C_{\dim_q}) has m_e baked into the formula. Empirically the bound–free differential vanishes for the atomic-braid \tau, so T_4 contributes no binding at this stage (open question — see remarks).
  • T_5 binding (chirality): per chirality dual-space derivation, T_5 = (a_K - 1) \cdot T_1 as a multiplicative correction on T_1. With T_1 in cat units and E_{0,\beta} as T_1's MeV scale, the binding contribution is E_{0,\beta} \cdot (a_K - 1) \cdot T_1^{\rm atom}.
  • T_6 binding (cyclotomic tail): per full pole structure, T_6 comes pre-converted to MeV via the canonical Habiro residue evaluation. No additional scaling needed.

The total B(Z, N) is the sum of these per-term contributions and is positive for bound systems. \square

Empirical verification.

The assembly is implemented in the formal derivation as assemble_per_derivation_weights(Z, N) with hardcoded constants E_{0,\beta} = 0.78233341 MeV (CODATA β-decay Q), \alpha = m_e \cdot 8G = 3.74446989 MeV, m_e = 0.510999\;\text{MeV} MeV. Across the proton..{}^{9}Be spectrum (12 atoms):

See Table 3.

Mean \lvert\delta\mathfrak{m}/\mathfrak{m}\rvert = 0.184\%, max = 0.525\% ({}^{4}He).

This matches the standalone the atomic-braid mass formula in the Particles chapter formula's empirical fit (0.13–0.16% mean across the same spectrum) and 76\times improves on the proton-fitted single-E_0 assembly (14.7% mean) — the improvement is entirely from honouring the per-term derivation weights.

Open questions.

  1. T_4 binding contribution vanishes empirically. The term4_frobenius_codim evaluation gives the same value for bound and free configurations, so the differential T_4^{\rm atom} - T_4^{\rm free} = 0 identically. Either T_4 is independent of inter-nucleon crossings by construction (in which case it cancels out of the binding formula and contributes only to the total mass via the Z\,m_{\mathfrak{p}} baseline), or the implementation is missing a coupling. Investigation pending.
  2. T_6 Habiro residue witness coverage. The _load_canonical_t6_MeV helper currently returns 0 for A \geq 5 atoms because the Habiro residue witness lacks data for them. Once populated, T_6 will start contributing to the heavier-atom predictions; expect {\sim}\,few-keV-level corrections per atom based on the A \leq 4 pattern.
  3. {}^{4}He outlier (0.525 %). Largest residual in the spectrum. Worth a focused look — possibly a missing T_4 contribution that would manifest only at the doubly-magic {}^{4}He configuration.
